title: WW3 Threat Assessment: World War III Has Quietly Started!
summary: Panel of a former CIA officer, a nuclear-war author and a historian argues WW3 has quietly begun as proxy, cyber and information war, and dwells on nuclear accident risk.

assertions.quote: I believe that we are already at the early stages if not in World War II.
we are one misunderstanding, one miscalculation away, or even one AI generated viral video from nuclear annihilation
I think this idea of kinetic warfare is less frequent especially among the major powers.

verdicts.note: Rivalry between the US, Russia and China runs through arms to third parties, cyber intrusions and influence campaigns, while they avoid fighting each other directly.

DoD describes China using coast guard and maritime militia coercion that is 'increasingly aggressive' but designed to assert claims 'while avoiding armed conflict'; this fits competition below war for China in its region, not great powers in general.

DDIS describes Russia's hybrid war of sabotage, cyber attacks and influence kept below armed conflict, used because open war would be too risky, but Russia is also fighting a conventional war in Ukraine.

US intelligence says many states are more willing to use deniable, coercive means below the threshold of war (sabotage, assassinations), but also warns Beijing and Moscow could respond with force, so direct conflict is not ruled out.
UCDP notes more states fighting interstate conflicts and militarily backing rebel groups, the proxy part of the claim; cyber and information operations are not measured.

The WEF's 2026 survey ranks geoeconomic confrontation first (18%) and state-based armed conflict second (14%), describing trade, finance and technology 'wielded as weapons'; misinformation and cyber insecurity are also in the top 10. Non-military competition leads, but the report stresses economic levers more than proxy wars.

assertions.quote: everyone at the Pentagon knows that no matter how nuclear war begins, it ends in total annihilation

verdicts.note: Escalation after first use is a serious risk in wargames, but there is no record of nuclear war and limited use need not lead to all-out exchange.
A linked Metaculus forecast puts the median number of nuclear weapons used by 2050, given any are used, at about 5, so forecasters expect a first use to stay limited rather than become all-out war.

FRI participants said a deliberate non-test detonation before 2030 would raise their probability of a 10-million-death catastrophe by 2045 4x (experts, from 5%) or 6.7x (superforecasters, from 1%), well short of certain escalation.
RAND says Russian nuclear use 'could be surprisingly extensive' once the taboo is broken, which supports escalation risk but is a possibility, not a finding that limited use would become all-out war.

assertions.quote: Tactical nuclear weapons are not are no longer in the US arsenal for precisely that reason

verdicts.note: The US still holds B61 gravity bombs, about a hundred of them deployed in Europe, and fielded the low-yield W76-2 warhead in 2020.

assertions.quote: it makes much more sense for them to hold their weapons and continue using it as a as a deterrent

verdicts.note: Clauset: the efforts since WWII to reduce large wars have not yet changed the statistics enough to tell whether they work, so the record cannot credit deterrence or any other mechanism.

The case file says most historians credit the threat of nuclear destruction for the Cold War never turning hot. Others point to geographic distance, reconnaissance that reduced misunderstandings, mutual limits on competition and arms-control cooperation, so deterrence is the leading explanation but not the only one.

Hanania notes that international-relations theorists hold that nuclear weapons made great-power war unthinkable. He warns that giving them the credit sets aside secularization, mass wealth, mass media, faster leader communication and satellite intelligence, so deterrence is one possible cause among several.

Metaculus's background says deterrence theory credits nuclear deterrence for 80 years of relative peace but notes the theory is contested and there is no expert consensus on how much deterrence explains it.

assertions.quote: the climate models that now tell us this very factually that humanity dies

verdicts.note: One 2022 model estimates about five billion deaths from famine after a US-Russia war, but the severity of nuclear winter is disputed and other models find far less cooling.

assertions.quote: 59 states um have erupted in war since 2023, which is the greatest number logged in any year since 1946

verdicts.note: Uppsala counted 61 state-based conflicts in 2024, the most since 1946, though most are civil wars rather than wars between states.
Citing PRIO, US intelligence counts 61 active state-based conflicts in 2024, the highest number since the end of the Second World War.
CFR's 2026 survey report states the number of armed conflicts is now at its highest since the end of World War II, with a growing share interstate.
UCDP counts 59 state-based conflicts in 2023 and 2024, then a record 65 in 2025, the highest since its data begin in 1946.
UCDP's press release: 65 conflicts involving states in 2025, the highest since records began in 1946, and 8 interstate conflicts, also the highest since 1946.
PRIO, using UCDP data: more than 50 state-based conflicts a year for 11 years, peaking at 65 in 2025; only the early 1990s came close since 1946.

Citing the 2025 Global Peace Index, the WEF report says more state-based armed conflicts are ongoing than at any time since the Second World War and that key conflict-risk indicators are at their worst levels since then.

assertions.quote: world military spending is up by about 10% year-over-year, which is the highest sum ever recorded by SIPAR

verdicts.note: SIPRI put 2024 world military spending at about 2.7 trillion dollars, the tenth straight annual rise and the steepest since the Cold War.
SIPRI: world military spending rose 2.9 percent in real terms to $2887 billion in 2025, the 11th consecutive annual rise and the highest level it has recorded, up 41 percent over 2016-25.

assertions.quote: in response they fired an intermediate range ballistic missile capable of carrying a nuclear warhead

verdicts.note: In November 2024 Russia struck Dnipro with the conventionally armed Oreshnik and said it had warned the US through the nuclear risk-reduction channel.
SIPRI reports Russia's dual-capable Oreshnik IRBM has been used against Ukraine with conventional warheads (most recently May 2026) and that Russia is building a forward base for it in Belarus.
US intelligence cites Russia's combat use of dual-capable intermediate-range ballistic missile systems in Ukraine.

assertions.quote: I just don't think Iran is the hill that the Russians or Chinese will die on.
So, now they have even more incentive to develop a nuclear weapon than they've ever had.

verdicts.note: Many analysts expect attacks to strengthen the case for a bomb inside Iran, but the same strikes destroy capacity and the regime's choice is not yet visible.
The Bulletin says it remains unclear whether the June 2025 strikes constrained Iran's effort or persuaded it to pursue nuclear weapons covertly.
